design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (debit_card_disputes_and_card_servicing)

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}. The tree has one prerequisite problem; each of the two computations declares 4 factors (liability: 4, final credit: 4). Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed: card_ext_takeover_card_liability (target file_unauthorized_card_dispute_b9450be9, owner=user) and card_ext_takeover_card_final_credit (target post_takeover_dispute_credit_edfadedb, owner=agent). Headroom left for task 1 (draw: 1 prerequisite, factors [4, 6]): the merchant-dispute side of the charter (incorrect-amount filing on a single-use virtual card and its on-filing credit), which shares no policy, tool or base mechanism claimed here (no takeover lock, no liability, no approval-on-filing).
Design thesis: surface goal "a virtual card I never made has a $389 charge; I want that money back" -> the policy that pays it (the takeover-card final credit) states that it is booked only after the purchase stands under an unauthorized dispute carrying its recorded liability -> that dispute is the customer's own filing, whose liability is itself a 4-factor computation -> the final credit (4 factors) is evaluated on the world after the filing. Depth: 2 problems, one value_input edge. Breadth: card ledger (purchase, fee, holds), card lifecycle dates, the dispute ledger, the linked personal account's lock record, plan, opening date and direct-deposit ledger (cross-difficulty wallet).
Why single-object: the compute DSL aggregates per card; a takeover card (a virtual card the customer never created) carries only the thief's activity, so "the card's settled purchases" is exactly the disputed purchase and the rule can say so honestly.

[Problem-tree card] root = card_ext_takeover_card_final_credit; prerequisite = card_ext_takeover_card_liability. Edge: kind value_input, gate disputed_open (also liability_open), form state. Prerequisite sentence (affirmative direction, the way a disputes desk states that a payout waits on the claim): "The final credit is booked only after the takeover card's purchase stands on the records with an open unauthorized dispute carrying its recorded customer liability." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; waits on a record-visible state (an open unauthorized dispute record with its liability on the card); names no tool, id or code token; strength "only after" = hard requirement, scope = the takeover card's purchase. Exactly one write of the difficulty brings that state about: the unauthorized filing (file_unauthorized_card_dispute_b9450be9) is the only write that creates a card_dispute_filed record of reason unauthorized; the other filing tool writes reason incorrect_amount. Derivation: sentence + records (find_card_disputes shows no dispute on the card ending 2658) + the liability policy's rule (it settles "the customer liability recorded when the cardholder disputes, as unauthorized, a purchase on a virtual card they say they never created") -> the customer's own unauthorized filing. Owner of the resolving write: user (the cardholder asserts his own rights, blueprint doctrine). False at the opening: initial_state.card_disputes holds only the 2025 duplicate-charge dispute on the physical card (card_txn_id = the physical card's purchase o2); nothing references the takeover purchase. Topological order: liability filing (step 8) -> final credit (step 10). Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping step 8 recomputes the credit to 23.89 instead of 410.89 (open disputed amount and liability both 0.00) and removes the filed dispute row. The persona never mentions a dispute or a claim; the credit tool does not check for one (it copies the filed record when present and writes anyway otherwise).

[Base-invariant card] Filing (subject card_dispute_filed): governing base policies card_disputes_unauthorized and card_disputes_merchant. Gates: card_blocked_first — the takeover card status is blocked (block_reason compromised, blocked 2026-09-15) -> holds. unauthorized_window — anchor card_transactions.txn_date 2026-09-13, Signature unauthorized_report_days 60, calendar days, inclusive: 2026-09-24 is day 11, last day 2026-11-12 accepted, 2026-11-13 refused. one_dispute_per_transaction — no dispute references the purchase. merchant_window — 120 days, same anchor, satisfied. merchant_contacted_first — retired by this policy's overwrite (a takeover-card dispute needs no merchant contact); the base gate concerns goods-not-received/not-as-described/credit-not-processed reasons only. Credit (subjects card_dispute_resolved, card_dispute_credit): no structured gate applies (policy_scope for both governing policies); base "The disputes team records approved or denied" and the provisional-credit sentence are superseded by the declared overwrite (approval on filing for a card with a recorded takeover lock).

[Business-object card] Target object: the 389.00 purchase PWC 8841 2630 on the virtual card ending 2658 (card_txn_id p1), settled 2026-09-13 against hold AUTH 5K2Q7M. Included in the liability's settled purchases: p1 only. Excluded: the 250.00 Orbit Luxe Goods hold (never settled, released 2026-09-19) — the near-miss for the "settled purchases" reading; the physical card's 2025 grocery purchases and their approved duplicate-charge dispute (another card). Correlation key written back: card_txn_id = p1 on both writes; the credit links source_txn_id = p1.

[Factor card — liability, 4 factors] (1) notice_start_date, method, multi-source, cross-difficulty wallet: tiers {takeover lock AND card issued <= 1 day before the lock -> count from recovered date} / {not that AND blocked compromised on/after the last settlement -> count from block date} / {otherwise -> from the latest settlement date}. World: restriction_reason suspected_account_takeover, restricted_at 2026-09-12T23:18:00, card issued 2026-09-12 (0 days) -> recovered 2026-09-15 -> 9 notice days. Baseline (settlement date 2026-09-13 -> 11 days) gives 24.00. (2) notice_cap_tier, parameter: <= 2 days -> liability_cap_timely; 3..10 days -> 50 percent of liability_cap_late; > 10 -> liability_cap_late. World 9 days -> 25.00; baseline (base rule: timely cap within 2 days, else late cap) gives 24.00. (3) deposit_relief_tier, parameter, cross-difficulty wallet: two-month direct deposits >= 2000.00 -> 0.6; >= 300.00 -> 0.8; else 1. World 2449.60 (2026-07-31, 08-14, 08-28, 09-11); near-miss: the 2026-07-17 deposit is outside the two months. Baseline gives 20.00. (4) block_relief_tier, parameter: blocked >= 3 days after issue -> 0.8; 1-2 days -> 0.9; same day -> 1. World 3 days -> 0.8; baseline gives 15.00. Result: MN(389.00, RND(25.00 x 0.6 x 0.8, 2)) = 12.00. All factors at baseline: 50.00.
[Factor card — final credit, 4 factors] (1) liability_absorption, method, multi-source, cross-difficulty wallet: {Onyx/Summit AND lock <= 1 day after issue -> absorb all} / {Plus/Prime AND lock <= 1 day after issue -> absorb up to 10.00} / {otherwise -> keep all}. World Prime, 0 days -> kept 2.00; baseline 400.89. (2) lock_courtesy_tier, parameter, cross wallet: lock >= 3 days -> 10.00; 1-2 days -> 5.00; else 0. World 3 days -> 10.00; baseline 400.89. (3) fee_return_tier, parameter: foreign fees AND Signature/Infinite/Metal -> whole fee; foreign fees on other tiers -> 50 percent; none -> 0. World 3.89 on Signature -> 3.89; baseline 407.00. (4) tenure_courtesy_tier, parameter, cross wallet: >= 60 months -> 10.00; >= 24 -> 5.00; else 0. World 70 months -> 10.00; baseline 400.89. Result 389.00 - 2.00 + 10.00 + 3.89 + 10.00 = 410.89; all baseline 377.00. No stamp decides a tier: every tier is derived from dates, the wallet lock record and ledgers.
Overrides (declared): small-dispute auto-credit sentence of card_disputes_unauthorized (in both policies: a takeover-card purchase is settled by these rules whatever its amount); liability sentence of card_disputes_unauthorized (business days -> calendar notice with the takeover anchor and reliefs); merchant-contact clause of card_disputes_merchant; provisional-credit and disputes-team sentences of card_disputes_unauthorized for takeover cards. Everything else inherited (one dispute per transaction, windows, blocked-card requirement).

[Seed] Customer Tobias Hargrove; personal account Pocketwire Prime opened 2020-11-09, lock suspected_account_takeover at 2026-09-12T23:18:00, recovered 2026-09-15, ledger_balance 3032.03 = 5 x 612.40 deposits - 3 x 9.99 plan fees; physical Signature card ending 2217 (active); virtual Signature card ending 2658 issued 2026-09-12, blocked compromised 2026-09-15. Card activity: hold 389.00 + purchase 389.00 + foreign fee 3.89 (1.00 percent) on the virtual card; hold 250.00 released on day 7; the physical card's 2025 duplicate grocery charge with its approved dispute and final credit (also the dedup evidence row). Automatic clauses checked: the released hold follows auth_hold_release_days 7; the foreign fee equals RND(389.00 x 1.00/100, 2); the old dispute is approved with its triggered credit; no pending obligation is left (no due provisional credit, no unreleased hold past its period, no plan fee due before 2026-10-12). No rewards membership, so the purchases trigger no points.

[Persona] Tired, plain-spoken dispatcher; volunteers only the surface goal (virtual card never made, 389 charge, wants the money back); gives phone, then DOB and ZIP when asked (SSN/email only if another detail is needed); confirms on request that the card and store are not his; says the 250 hold was not his but he is not worried if it never charged; files in his own name when the agent hands the step over; closes when told the money is credited. No template labels; no mention of disputes, liability or order.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB, ZIP) -> find_card_accounts -> find_card_transactions -> find_card_disputes -> find_wallet_accounts -> find_wallet_transactions -> unlock+call (user) file_unauthorized_card_dispute_b9450be9(card ending 2658, purchase p1, dispute_amount 389.00, customer_liability 12.00) -> unlock+call post_takeover_dispute_credit_edfadedb(credit_amount 410.89).
[Verification run] Authoring evaluator (same primitives as check_compute) printed: liability (12.0, {notice_start_date: 24.0, notice_cap_tier: 24.0, deposit_relief_tier: 20.0, block_relief_tier: 15.0}, 50.0); credit (410.89, {liability_absorption: 400.89, lock_courtesy_tier: 400.89, fee_return_tier: 407.0, tenure_courtesy_tier: 400.89}, 377.0); credit with step 8 skipped (23.89, ...). Per-task gates run: check_extended/check_task_tools/replay_tasks/check_solvability/check_compute/check_grounding/check_cross_fire --task 0 (results recorded in the difficulty worklog.md).
[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Masking compute and gold: the KB will carry the takeover-card liability rule (notice start, notice cap, deposit relief, block relief) and the final-credit rule with its prerequisite sentence; the finders return the lock record, deposits, card dates and ledger. Reading them gives: must the credit wait? yes (no dispute on the card); who files? the customer (a dispute asserting his own rights); liability 12.00; credit 410.89 — identical to gold. Easily-missed points: counting notice from the settlement date (24.00 / 400.89 path), counting the released 250 hold as settled activity, including the 2026-07-17 deposit (no change here, tier still high), paying the credit before the filing (23.89), or posting a provisional credit instead of a final one.
[Rework r2] F1 (policy audit): both claimed policies left base card_disputes_unauthorized's small-dispute auto-credit sentence in force for a takeover purchase at or below small_dispute_auto_credit_threshold. Each now declares it superseded in `overwrite`, with a new rule sentence (liability policy: the liability is recorded whatever the amount, with no liability-free small-dispute credit; final-credit policy: the dispute is settled by the final credit whatever the amount). On this world the disputed 389.00 is above the 25.00 Signature threshold, so gold, baselines and sensitivities are unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Tobias Hargrove, a 40-year-old freight dispatcher in Chicago who uses Pocketwire for his paycheck and everyday spending. You are tired and a little rattled, but polite, and you talk in short, plain sentences. Somebody broke into your Pocketwire account last week; Pocketwire locked it and you got access back on the 15th. Going through the cards screen afterwards you found a virtual card ending 2658 that you never made, and on it a $389 charge from an electronics store in Shenzhen. You open the call by saying roughly: "Somebody got into my account last week, and there's a virtual card on it I never made, with a $389 charge on it. I want that money back." You do not know how Pocketwire handles this and you never suggest a procedure. When the agent asks who you are, you give your mobile number 5552627305 first; when asked for more you give your date of birth, 1986-07-22, and your home ZIP code, 60614. Only if the agent says it still needs another detail do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 2941, or your email, tobias.hargrove@pw2mail.example. If the agent asks, you confirm that you never created the card ending 2658, never shopped at that store, and never gave your login or phone to anyone; your own card is the physical one ending 2217, which you still have. If the agent asks about a $250 hold from Orbit Luxe Goods on that virtual card, you say it was not you either, but if it dropped off without charging you, you are not worried about it. If the agent explains that you yourself have to put the claim in, or confirm it, in your own name, you agree right away, and when the agent hands the step to you, you carry it out exactly as the agent lays it out and read back whatever confirmation comes up. You do not know what share of the charge, if any, you might have to carry, and you do not argue about any figure the agent gives you. Once the agent tells you the money has been credited back to the card, you say thanks, that is all you needed, and you end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: An unauthorized dispute is filed only on a card whose status is blocked or closed, so a card still active or locked must be blocked as compromised first.
the dispute is filed no later than unauthorized_report_days calendar days after the disputed card transaction's date

the dispute is filed no later than merchant_dispute_days calendar days after the card transaction date

base_preconditions.condition: Outcome and dispute credit of an unauthorized dispute: no structured gate applies to the outcome or the final credit; the takeover-card rule approves on filing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona says only that a card he never made carries a 389 charge and that he wants the money back; it never mentions a dispute, a claim to be filed first, a liability or any ordering. It agrees to file in its own name only after the agent explains that step.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_takeover_dispute_credit_edfadedb in task_tools.py never checks for a filed dispute: it copies the filed record's fields when one exists and otherwise writes the outcome and credit anyway, returning a normal receipt; file_unauthorized_card_dispute_b9450be9 checks no card status, window or duplicate.
